podcast.title: Consistent Earnings from Touring (2016)
podcast.body: Adele is a perennial presence on the Forbes list, consistently ranking between positions 10 and 20. Her income is primarily derived from a continuous system of concerts and tours. "tienen un sistema de conciertos y gira de manera continuada, que es de prácticamente donde ingresan todo su dinero."

podcast.title: Adele World Temporary Residency (2024)
podcast.body: In 2024, Live Nation constructed a temporary pop-up stadium in Munich capable of holding 80,000 people, creating "Adele World." During this unique residency, Adele performed twice a week for a month, drawing 730,000 attendees. The event broke the record for a non-Vegas residency, grossing $240 million USD over just 10 shows and injecting half a billion euros into Munich's economy that month. "They created Adele World, a place where she could perform twice a week for a month."

podcast.title: Authentic Public Image
podcast.body: Adele cultivates an image of authenticity and relatability, exemplified by her actions. Following the Grenfell fire disaster in London, she personally visited a local fire station, bringing cake for the firefighters as a gesture of gratitude. "After the Grenfell fire disaster in London, she showed up at a local fire station with some cake for the firefighters, just as a way of saying thanks."

podcast.body: Adele's vinyl records, despite strong sales, are not anticipated to maintain high collector's value in the long term, as her audience is not typically composed of demanding collectors, and her albums are expected to depreciate significantly over 15-20 years. podcast.title: Opposition to Trump Campaign Music Use
podcast.body: Adele was among a long list of artists who expressed strong opposition to Donald Trump's campaign using their music at political rallies. Despite venues often holding blanket performing rights licenses, artists did not want their work associated with the campaign and many pursued cease and desist orders or lawsuits. "The list of artists against Trump using their music is long."

podcast.title: Pop Dominance in 2010s
podcast.body: Adele was a major pop artist whose popularity contributed to the overall rise of pop music that "swamped" rock by 2011 or 2012, signifying the genre's significant cultural influence during the decade. "And you can make the argument that it certainly did swamp by not only a rise in pop music, you know, Maroon 5, Justin Bieber, Rihanna, Pink Kitty Perry, Carly Recepcion, Adele, but also by the increasing strength of hip hop and the big beats and bass lines of EDM."

podcast.title: Road Rage Treatment
podcast.body: Scientists in Brazil found that listening to instrumental versions of Adele's songs, particularly piano versions of "Someone Like You" and "Hello," can help reduce road rage. This research is significant due to the high number of road fatalities in Brazil, with nearly 50,000 people dying on the road each year. "The study determined that piano versions of someone like you and hello work best."

xref.title: Dan Wilson's Songwriting Prowess
xref.body: Guitarist and singer Dan Wilson has achieved considerable recognition as a highly sought-after professional songwriter. He co-wrote Adele's massive global hit "Someone Like You," which topped charts in dozens of countries and earned him a Grammy for Song of the Year. He also received a Grammy for his production work on Adele's "21" album and was nominated for a Grammy for writing "Not Ready to Make Nice" for the Dixie Chicks. His extensive songwriting credits include collaborations with dozens of other notable acts, such as Fantagram, John Legend, Steve Perry, Josh Groban, Jason Barraiz, Leanne Rhyme, Stevie Nick's Halsey Cold War Kids, K-Flay, Weezer, Panic at the Disco, and Taylor Swift. "But the big story here is guitarist and singer Dan Wilson. He's become a renowned songwriter for hire."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Great Alt-Rock One-Hit Wonders of the 90s: Part 1

xref.title: Dolores O'Riordan's Impact
xref.body: Dolores O'Riordan, the face and voice of The Cranberries, possessed a powerful and unique vocal style, recognized as one of the most distinctive in the history of alternative rock. She was a significant influence on contemporary artists like Adele, Florence Welch, and Halsey. "Her powerful vocal style was unique and has been called one of the most distinctive voices in the history of Al Rock. Talk to Adele or Florence Welcher, Hallsley, and they'll tell you that Dolores was a huge influence on them."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: Women Who Rocked The 90's

xref.title: Successful Songwriting Career
xref.body: After his success with Semisonic, Dan Wilson has had a highly lucrative career as a songwriter, earning "real money." He penned at least six songs for The Dixie Chicks (including a Grammy winner for Song of the Year), three songs for Adele's *21* album (including "Someone Like You"), and co-written with numerous other major artists such as Taylor Swift, Tom Morello, Celine Dion, John Legend, and Pink. "But it is as a songwriter where Dan has made the real money."
